   City Council Minutes - Study Session
  City of Westlake Village  March 23, 2022  2

  STUDY SESSION:

  1.  DISCUSSION ON THE CITY'S LEGISLATIVE PLATFORM AND THE 2022
  CALIFORNIA LEGISLATIVE SESSION

  City Manager de Geus introduced the item, stating that the City has been more  =
  engaged in the legislative process in the past few years and has retained the
  Renne Public Policy Group (RPPG) as the City's legislative advisors. He noted
  that RPPG will provide an update on the legislative calendar, briefly discuss the
  City of Westlake Village's Legislative Platform, the Governor's budget, and bills
  that are being monitored during this session.

  Mr. de Geus mentioned that on March 14, 2022, the Administrative Committee,
  comprised of Mayor Halpern and Mayor Pro Tern Pearl, reviewed this topic. He
  noted that Deputy City Manager Eskandar is the lead staff member on the City's
  legislative matters.

  Deputy City Manager Eskandar introduced Ms. Sharon Gonsalves, Director of
  Government Affairs with RPPG. He noted that Ms. Gonsalves will be attending
  the meeting virtually as she is in Sacramento where she is continuing her
  engagement in legislative committee meetings.

  Ms. Gonsalves led the presentation and introduced her core team that includes
  Dane Hutchings and Alyssa Silhi. She reviewed the critical dates in the 2022
  legislative calendar, noting that this is the second year of a two-year term.

  Mr. Eskandar noted that the Council adopted the Legislative Platform with several
  policy areas of focus which would be the highest priority for the City. The policy
  areas included:
  • Local Control
  • Public Safety
  • Fiscal Responsibility
  • Contract City Authority
  • Environment & Sustainability
  • Technology

  He highlighted that RPPG is focused on a subset of these policy areas specific to:
  land use and housing; public safety; and, environmental and sustainability. He
  noted that while those are the main focus areas, RPPG holds regular updates with
  staff where they provide a variety of information on several legislative matters of
  interest that are happening in Sacramento and staff provides them with status
  updates from the City .

 ___________________________
._  -  ~  -  -·

  City of Westlake Village  March 23, 2022  3

  Ms. Gonsalves stated that RPPG reviewed the City's Legislative Platform adopted
  in 2021 and is not recommending any modifications at this time. RPPG will review

l  it again this fall before the 2023-2024 legislative session begins and if needed,
  make recommendations for any changes to the City's Legislative Platform. Ms.
  Gonsalves then provided an overview of the Governor's proposed budget and
  timeline, the State legislative priorities, and highlighted bills that RPPG will be
  monitoring during the remainder of the legislative session as they fall into the four
  main policy areas of focus; land use and housing; public safety; and, environmental
  and sustainability. Finally, she provided an update on redistricting maps, the
  California Business Round Table ballot initiative, and next steps in the remaining
  legislative process.

  Mr. Eskandar reviewed the City's legislative calendar and informed the City
  Council that this would be the first of two study sessions.

  Mayor Pro Tern Pearl emphasized that the purpose of the Legislative Platform is
  to allow staff to work with current legislators on funding requests for projects. The
  City would stand better opportunities to receive funding if our projects can be tied
  into a Governor's initiative or areas of statewide significance. Councilmember
  Davis concurred and noted the need to come up with specific projects that would
  deliver a financial benefit to the City.

  Ms. Gonsalves thanked the City Council for their input. Deputy City Manager
  Eskandar shared that efforts to develop relations with legislators can benefit the
  City with future funding opportunities as legislators learn more about the City and
  advocate for specific carve-outs such as those that benefit small populations. He
  noted that in many cases, Westlake doesn't meet the funding requirements, as it
  is not a disadvantaged or rural community. Showing that small population
  communities need funding may help in the future.

  City Manager de Geus noted that rather than oppose legislation, he would explore
  opportunities to partner with legislators to accomplish shared values that fit within
  the context of Westlake Village.

  Councilmember Davis mentioned that it would be beneficial if we could join efforts

j  with neighboring cities, either in Los Angeles or Ventura County, which have
  relationships to one another and would benefit from regional opportunities such as
  broadband. Rather than look at projects within our boundaries, we could be
  leaders in our area and collectively seek assistance from our legislators in
  Sacramento.

  Mayor Halpern acknowledged that legislators do forget about the small cities, and
  we do need funding, especially Federal funding, which tends to be earmarked for
  the large and disadvantaged cities.
